Niseko is full of rowdy Australians :-(

One thing this article doesn't cover is that the Austrlians took a ski resort that went bankrupt and bought it. They also heavily invested in the area of Niseko building bars and restaurants.

This article totally skips the point that Niseko has and is one of the top places to ski in the world. Powder snow and because of its location it really is a place you can ski off post and find really nuggets of happiness.

The Ainu were actually from down south too but driven off the main island which has Osaka and Tokyo. The Ainu are many ways like North American Indians but a big difference you notice is that have body hair.

Comparing Susukino in Sapporo to Tokyo shit holes is a complete joke! Susukino covers blocks and blocks of the city compared to shitty ass Tokyo -- Roppongi is complete shit! It sucks donkey balls compared to Susukino!

Hokkaido is heavily influenced by American consultants. The university of Holkaido is the oldest in the Country and is based on the one in Amherst Massachusets. It is ranked number 5 of all national universities.

Sapporo beer is also directly related to the University. Sapporo beer also is the origins of Asahi beer and possibly Kirin (I don't refer exact). Yes, these beers are essentially American with a Japanese twist.

The article mentions the Bullet Train coming to Hakodate which is rather close to the northern part of the main island. The article doesn't cover the fact that it will go through a tunnel under the straight and if I remember correctly is the longest and possibly deepest in the world. This alone is completely amazing! Currently normal express trains already do this.

The man New Chirose airport is also amazing! Chocolate and Doreamon Musuem is in the new wing. Although Chitose is a piss ant town it is still 60,000 people living there.

Yes, those famous people have used Holkaido as a place to reference but beware traveler!

You do not go to Hokkaido to find Japan!

You go to Hokkaido to a wonderful blend of nature, western like Japan. It's not flashy and shitty like Tokyo but it's an island full of people who are down to earth and really understand what it's like to live on such a beautiful island.

In the Summer Hokkaido makes you think you are in Europe with all kinds of university kids bicycling around the island or those motor cycle groups going from one biker house to the next. Hokkaido isn't huge but going from one side of the island to the next will take you around 12 hours by car. Trains also cover the majority of towns and villages so that's possible too.

Just be prepared to not find samurai or geisha. This island just doesn't do that.
